title: Long-term effects of daily VR use on vision
bottleneck: Nobody knows what hours-daily VR does to developing or adult eyes over years: myopia progression, binocular vision changes, and dry-eye effects are plausible but unstudied at scale. Vergence-accommodation conflict's chronic impact is unknown, and children's use is effectively an uncontrolled experiment. Longitudinal data doesn't exist because the behavior is new.
why_it_blocks: Health uncertainty is a liability for schools, employers, and parents considering all-day VR. Without long-term safety data, institutional adoption stays cautious.
current_state: Short-term studies show transient eyestrain and focus changes; manufacturers add comfort warnings and age guidance. Definitive longitudinal research is still pending. Chronic effects of vergence-accommodation conflict are unstudied, leaving schools and employers to guess at the long-term risks. Manufacturers' age guidance is precautionary rather than evidence-based, because the longitudinal evidence simply does not exist yet.
